title: Solitaire Engagement Rings
rule: tag = Engagement Rings AND tag = Solitaire
seo_description: Solitaire engagement rings with one center diamond in round, oval, emerald, marquise and radiant cuts. Free insured shipping and 14-day returns.
intro: A solitaire engagement ring holds one center diamond on a plain or lightly set band, so the stone's shape and cut carry the design. Laura Milman New York offers lab-grown diamond solitaires in round, oval, emerald, marquise, cushion and radiant shapes, in prong, bezel and half-bezel settings.
guide_html:
What makes a ring a solitaire

A solitaire has a single center diamond. The band may be plain or carry small accent diamonds, but nothing competes with the center stone.

Prong, bezel or half bezel

Prongs hold the diamond with small metal claws and let the most light reach the stone. A bezel wraps the stone in a rim of metal, which protects the edge and sits lower on the hand. A half bezel covers two sides and leaves two open.

Choosing the shape

Round cuts return the most sparkle. Oval, marquise and pear shapes look longer on the finger for their carat weight. Emerald and radiant cuts show a step-cut or crushed-ice look. Compare loose stones in lab-grown diamonds or natural diamonds, or build your own in the ring builder.

faq.question: What is a solitaire engagement ring?
faq.answer: A solitaire engagement ring has one center diamond and no side stones competing with it. The band can be plain or have small accent diamonds.

faq.question: Which diamond shapes come in a solitaire setting?
faq.answer: This collection includes round, oval, emerald, marquise, step marquise, cushion and radiant solitaires. Each listing names its shape and metal.

faq.question: Is a prong or bezel setting better for a solitaire?
faq.answer: Prongs show more of the diamond and let in more light. A bezel protects the stone's edge and sits lower, which suits an active lifestyle.

faq.question: Can I choose my own diamond for a solitaire?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose a setting in engagement ring settings or use the ring builder, then pick a loose natural or lab-grown diamond. Setting labor is included.

faq.question: What is the return policy?
faq.answer: Engagement rings ship free and insured, with 14-day returns.

title: Hidden Halo Engagement Rings
rule: tag = Engagement Rings AND tag = Hidden Halo
seo_title: Hidden Halo Engagement Rings | Laura Milman
seo_description: Hidden halo engagement rings with a row of diamonds under the center stone, seen from the side. Lab-grown diamonds. Free insured shipping and 14-day returns.
intro: A hidden halo engagement ring has a thin row of small diamonds set beneath the center stone, visible from the side but not from above. From the top it reads as a solitaire. Laura Milman New York offers lab-grown hidden halo rings in round, oval, emerald and radiant shapes, in white and yellow gold.
guide_html:
Hidden halo vs. halo

A classic halo circles the center diamond on top, so the stone looks larger from above. A hidden halo sits under the stone at the basket, so the top view stays clean and the diamonds show when the hand turns.

Shapes in this collection

Round, oval, emerald and radiant centers. Each listing names its shape, metal and carat weight.

Pairing with a band

Because the halo sits under the stone, most straight wedding bands can sit flush against a hidden halo ring.

faq.question: What is a hidden halo engagement ring?
faq.answer: A hidden halo ring has small diamonds set in a ring under the center stone. They are seen from the side, while the top view looks like a solitaire.

faq.question: What is the difference between a halo and a hidden halo?
faq.answer: A halo frames the center stone on top. A hidden halo sits below it, so the ring keeps a solitaire look from above.

faq.question: Will a wedding band sit flush with a hidden halo ring?
faq.answer: Usually, yes. The halo sits under the center stone rather than at band level, so most straight bands sit close against it.

faq.question: Are these diamonds lab-grown?
faq.answer: The hidden halo rings in this collection are lab-grown diamond rings. Each listing states the origin of its stones.

intro: A halo engagement ring surrounds the center stone with a frame of small diamonds, which makes the center look larger and adds sparkle from above. guide_html:
Why choose a halo

The frame of small diamonds catches light around the center stone and makes it read larger on the hand than its carat weight alone.

Halo with a colored center

A white diamond halo around a fancy-color diamond sharpens the contrast of the center color. See more in fancy color diamond engagement rings.

Prefer a cleaner top view?

A hidden halo moves the diamonds under the stone.

faq.question: What is a halo engagement ring?
faq.answer: A halo ring has a row of small diamonds encircling the center stone on top, framing it and adding sparkle.

faq.question: Does a halo make the diamond look bigger?
faq.answer: Yes. The halo widens the area of sparkle around the center, so the stone reads larger from above than it would as a solitaire.

faq.question: Do you have halo rings with colored diamonds?
faq.answer: Yes. This collection includes fancy-color diamond halo rings. Each listing names the center color, shape and metal.

faq.question: What is the return policy?
faq.answer: Engagement rings ship free and insured, with 14-day returns.

title: Three-Stone Engagement Rings
rule: tag = Engagement Rings AND tag = Three Stone
seo_description: Three-stone engagement rings with a center diamond and two side stones, in round, oval, pear and marquise. Free insured shipping and 14-day returns.
intro: A three-stone engagement ring sets a center diamond between two side stones, usually smaller and often a contrasting shape. Laura Milman New York offers lab-grown three-stone rings with round, oval, pear and marquise diamonds in gold, each listing naming its center shape and metal.
guide_html:
How a three-stone ring is built

The center stone sets the size and shape. The side stones can match it or contrast it, such as pear or marquise sides next to a round or oval center.

What the three stones mean

The design is often read as past, present and future. It is also simply a way to add width and sparkle across the finger.

Pairing with a band

Three-stone rings sit wider than a solitaire. A straight or slightly curved wedding band is the usual partner.

faq.question: What is a three-stone engagement ring?
faq.answer: A three-stone ring has a center diamond with one side stone on each side, set in a row across the band.

faq.question: What do the three stones symbolize?
faq.answer: They are traditionally read as past, present and future.

faq.question: Can the side stones be a different shape?
faq.answer: Yes. Side stones often contrast the center, such as pear or marquise sides next to a round or oval center.

faq.question: Are these diamonds lab-grown?
faq.answer: The three-stone rings in this collection are lab-grown diamond rings. Each listing states the origin of its stones.

title: East-West Engagement Rings
rule: tag = Engagement Rings AND tag = East-West
seo_description: East-west engagement rings with an elongated diamond set sideways across the finger, in emerald, marquise and radiant. Free insured shipping and 14-day returns.
intro: An east-west engagement ring sets an elongated diamond sideways, so its long side runs across the finger instead of along it. Laura Milman New York offers lab-grown east-west rings with emerald, marquise and radiant diamonds in gold, in prong, bezel and half-bezel settings.
guide_html:
East-west vs. north-south

Most elongated diamonds are set north-south, pointing up the finger. East-west turns the same stone ninety degrees for a wider, lower look that stacks well with bands.

Shapes that suit it

Emerald, marquise, radiant, oval and pear cuts work because they are longer than they are wide. Round and square stones look the same either way.

Build your own

Pick an elongated stone in lab-grown diamonds and ask a specialist about an east-west setting.

faq.question: What is an east-west engagement ring?
faq.answer: An east-west ring sets an elongated diamond horizontally, so its long side runs across the finger.

faq.question: Which diamond shapes work east-west?
faq.answer: Elongated shapes such as emerald, marquise, radiant, oval and pear. This collection includes emerald, marquise and radiant.

faq.question: Do east-west rings stack with wedding bands?
faq.answer: Yes. The sideways stone sits lower and wider, which lines up well with straight bands.

faq.question: Are these diamonds lab-grown?
faq.answer: The east-west rings in this collection are lab-grown diamond rings. Each listing states the origin of its stones.

guide_html:
How color is graded

Fancy-color diamonds are graded by hue and intensity, from Fancy Light through Fancy, Fancy Intense and Fancy Vivid. When a stone shows two colors, the main hue is named last, as in brownish pink. Each listing gives the color as graded.

Cut and color

Radiant and cushion cuts are common for colored diamonds because their faceting deepens the color. The metal matters too: yellow gold under a yellow diamond and rose gold under a pink one strengthen the face-up color.

Loose colored diamonds

See fancy yellow diamonds, fancy pink diamonds and colored lab-grown diamonds.

faq.question: What is a fancy color diamond?
faq.answer: A fancy color diamond has a distinct body color, such as yellow, pink, green or gray, beyond the normal color scale for white diamonds.

faq.question: What do Fancy Light, Fancy Intense and Fancy Vivid mean?
faq.answer: They are intensity grades, from lighter to stronger color. Each listing states the color grade of its center diamond.

faq.question: Why are some rings set in two metals?
faq.answer: White metal holds the side diamonds while yellow or rose gold sits under the center, which strengthens the color of the stone.

faq.question: What is the return policy?

title: Oval Engagement Rings
rule: tag = Engagement Rings AND tag = Oval
seo_description: Oval diamond engagement rings in solitaire, hidden halo and three-stone settings, lab-grown and fancy color. Free insured shipping and 14-day returns.
intro: An oval engagement ring has an elongated, brilliant-cut center diamond that looks larger on the finger than a round diamond of the same carat weight. Laura Milman New York offers oval rings in solitaire, hidden halo, half-bezel and three-stone settings, with lab-grown and fancy-color diamonds.
guide_html:
Why ovals look larger

An oval spreads its carat weight over a longer outline, so its top face is larger than a round of the same weight. The length also makes the finger look longer.

Length-to-width ratio

Ovals are usually between 1.30 and 1.50 long for every 1 wide. A lower ratio looks fuller; a higher one looks slimmer.

The bow-tie

Many ovals show a darker bow-tie shape across the center. Check the video on each listing, or compare loose lab-grown ovals in the ring builder.

faq.question: Does an oval diamond look bigger than a round?
faq.answer: Yes. At the same carat weight an oval has a larger top surface and a longer outline, so it reads larger on the hand.

faq.question: What is a good length-to-width ratio for an oval?
faq.answer: Most ovals fall between 1.30 and 1.50. Lower ratios look fuller and higher ratios look slimmer.

faq.question: What is the bow-tie in an oval diamond?
faq.answer: It is a darker band across the middle of some ovals caused by how light passes through the stone. Well-cut ovals keep it faint.

faq.question: Which settings come with an oval center?
faq.answer: This collection includes oval solitaire, hidden halo, half-bezel, halo and three-stone rings.

intro: A round engagement ring holds a round brilliant diamond, the cut with the most facets aimed at returning light, which makes it the most sparkling diamond shape. Laura Milman New York offers round diamond rings in solitaire, hidden halo, three-stone and infinity settings, with lab-grown and natural diamonds in white and yellow gold.
guide_html:
Why round brilliants sparkle most

A round brilliant has 57 or 58 facets arranged to send light back through the top of the stone. Cut grade matters more on a round than on any other shape.

Settings for a round diamond

Four or six prongs are the classic solitaire. A hidden halo adds a ring of diamonds under the stone, and a three-stone adds a side stone on each side.

Choose your own diamond

Compare loose lab-grown and natural round diamonds, then pair one with a setting in the ring builder.

faq.question: Why are round diamonds the most popular engagement ring shape?
faq.answer: Round brilliants are cut to return the most light, so they show the most sparkle, and they suit every setting style.

faq.question: Four prongs or six prongs?
faq.answer: Four prongs show more of the diamond and look slightly square. Six prongs hold the stone more securely and keep a round outline.

faq.question: Which settings come with a round center?
faq.answer: This collection includes round solitaire, hidden halo, three-stone and infinity rings.

faq.question: Is engraving included?
faq.answer: Engraving is complimentary on engagement rings. Add your inscription on the product page.

seo_title: Emerald Cut Engagement Rings | Laura Milman
seo_description: Emerald cut diamond engagement rings in solitaire, hidden halo, bezel and east-west settings. Free insured shipping and 14-day returns.
intro: An emerald cut engagement ring holds a rectangular, step-cut diamond with long parallel facets and cut corners, which shows clarity and flashes of light rather than scattered sparkle. Laura Milman New York offers emerald cut rings in solitaire, hidden halo, bezel and east-west settings, in white and yellow gold.
guide_html:
Step cut vs. brilliant cut

Emerald cuts have long, flat facets in steps, like a staircase. They show broad flashes of light and a clear view into the stone, where a brilliant cut scatters small points of sparkle.

Clarity matters more

The open facets make inclusions easier to see, so emerald cuts are usually chosen at a higher clarity than round diamonds.

Not the gemstone

"Emerald cut" names the diamond's shape, not an emerald gemstone. Compare loose emerald cut stones in lab-grown diamonds.

faq.question: Is an emerald cut ring made with an emerald?
faq.answer: No. Emerald cut is a rectangular diamond shape with step facets. The rings in this collection have diamond centers.

faq.question: Do emerald cut diamonds sparkle?
faq.answer: They show broad flashes of light rather than the scattered sparkle of a round brilliant, with a clear, glassy look.

faq.question: What clarity should an emerald cut be?
faq.answer: Because the facets are open, inclusions are easier to see. Many buyers choose VS clarity or higher for an emerald cut.

faq.question: Which settings come with an emerald cut center?
faq.answer: This collection includes emerald cut solitaire, hidden halo, bezel and east-west rings.

title: Marquise Engagement Rings

seo_description: Marquise and step marquise diamond engagement rings in solitaire, east-west and three-stone settings. Free insured shipping and 14-day returns.
intro: A marquise engagement ring holds a long, boat-shaped diamond with pointed ends, the shape with the largest top face for its carat weight. Laura Milman New York offers lab-grown marquise rings in brilliant, step and Dutch marquise cuts, in solitaire, east-west and three-stone settings, in white, yellow and two-tone gold.
guide_html:
Marquise cuts in this collection

The brilliant marquise has classic sparkle. The step marquise has long step facets for a cleaner, glassy look. The Dutch and antique marquise use older-style faceting with a softer outline.

Protecting the points

The two tips are the most delicate part of the stone, so marquise settings use V-shaped prongs or a bezel at each point.

Wearing it

Set north-south, a marquise lengthens the finger. Set east-west, it sits low and wide.

faq.question: What is a marquise diamond?
faq.answer: A marquise is a long diamond with two pointed ends and curved sides. It has the largest top surface of any shape for its carat weight.

faq.question: What is a step marquise?
faq.answer: A step marquise has long step facets instead of brilliant facets, giving a cleaner, glassy look.

faq.question: Are marquise diamonds fragile?
faq.answer: The points are the vulnerable part, so they are held by V-prongs or a bezel. Set this way, a marquise wears well every day.

faq.question: Are these diamonds lab-grown?
faq.answer: The marquise rings in this collection are lab-grown diamond rings. Each listing states the origin and carat weight.

seo_description: Pear shaped diamond engagement rings with white, pink and yellow diamonds in gold and platinum. Free insured shipping and 14-day returns.
intro: A pear shaped engagement ring holds a teardrop diamond, round at one end and pointed at the other, which combines the sparkle of a round brilliant with the length of a marquise. Laura Milman New York offers pear rings with natural, lab-grown and fancy-color diamonds in white gold, yellow gold and platinum.
guide_html:
Which way the point faces

Most pear rings are worn with the point toward the fingertip, which lengthens the hand. Point toward the wrist is a less common choice.

Symmetry

A well-cut pear has even shoulders and a point lined up with the center of the rounded end. Check the video on each listing.

Side stones

Pear diamonds also appear as side stones in three-stone rings.

faq.question: Which way should a pear engagement ring point?
faq.answer: Traditionally the point faces the fingertip, which makes the finger look longer. Either direction is a matter of taste.

faq.question: Does a pear diamond look bigger than a round?
faq.answer: Yes. Its elongated outline gives a larger top face than a round diamond of the same carat weight.

faq.question: How is the point of a pear protected?
faq.answer: With a V-shaped prong or a bezel at the tip.

faq.question: Do you have colored pear diamond rings?
faq.answer: Yes. This collection includes fancy pink and fancy yellow pear diamond rings alongside white diamonds.

title: Radiant Cut Engagement Rings

seo_description: Radiant cut diamond engagement rings in lab-grown and fancy-color diamonds, solitaire to hidden halo. Free insured shipping and 14-day returns.
intro: A radiant cut engagement ring holds a rectangular or square diamond with trimmed corners and brilliant faceting, combining the outline of an emerald cut with the sparkle of a round. Laura Milman New York offers radiant rings with lab-grown and fancy-color diamonds in solitaire, hidden halo and east-west settings.
guide_html:
Radiant vs. emerald cut

Both have a rectangular outline with cut corners. The emerald cut uses step facets for flashes of light; the radiant uses brilliant facets for a crushed-ice sparkle.

Radiant and color

The radiant's faceting deepens body color, which is why many yellow, pink and green diamonds are cut this way. See fancy color diamond engagement rings.

Durable corners

Trimmed corners make the radiant less likely to chip than a princess cut.

faq.question: What is a radiant cut diamond?
faq.answer: A radiant is a rectangular or square diamond with trimmed corners and brilliant faceting, giving a lively, crushed-ice sparkle.

faq.question: What is the difference between radiant and emerald cut?
faq.answer: They share a cut-corner rectangular outline. Emerald cuts use step facets; radiants use brilliant facets and sparkle more.

faq.question: Why are many colored diamonds radiant cut?
faq.answer: Radiant faceting intensifies a diamond's body color, so it is a common cut for yellow, pink and green diamonds.

faq.question: Which settings come with a radiant center?
faq.answer: This collection includes radiant solitaire, half-bezel east-west and hidden halo rings, plus fancy-color radiant rings.
